Look at the picture of the para-archer and SHARE YOUR OBSERVATIONS with classmates and teacher. An oral task in a social context, C-1.1. Not C-2.2-LO-20: that outcome is about visual IMAGERY in the writing, not about describing an actual photograph.

'Does this personality inspire you? Explain how' -- the answer turns on her shooting with her feet because she has no arms, i.e. ability read past disability. C-2.2-LO-22. Not LO-21: no incident of the narrative is cited, the point is the capability itself.

Give a caption for the picture -- short, purposeful writing of the creative-slogan kind that C-1.3 names. Neither C-1.3 LO fits (LO-5 is a notice, LO-6 is a spoken piece on empathy), so competency level. DEFECT: the answer runs straight into 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube' and then into another item's answer about the silver medal in shot-put.

Extract on the Paralympics challenging stereotypes; the analogy sub-question completes to the word 'stereotypes' and the rest asks how the speaker pushed past the limits set for her. C-2.2-LO-22 exactly. Not LO-23: no fact-versus-opinion sorting is asked.

How Dr Malik's achievements CHALLENGE SOCIETAL PERCEPTIONS -- the stereotype-breaking clause of C-2.2-LO-22. Not C-2.1-LO-10, which concerns how the account records a change in attitudes over decades rather than how one athlete's record refutes an assumption.

The long-term impact of youth advocacy on disability -- the student reasons forward from the text to a consequence it does not state, which is C-3.2. Not C-2.2-LO-22, whose wording is 'how THE TEXT argues'; here the argument is the student's own.

Justify the title from Dr Malik's attitude and achievements -- the spine tumour at 29, the refusal to live in remorse, setbacks as stepping stones. Themes of resilience drawn from specific incidents, C-2.2-LO-21. Not LO-22: the question is about her response to adversity, not about stereotypes.

'Every setback is an opportunity to prove your strength' -- how this is a lesson for EVERY individual, not just sportspersons. Generalising a claim beyond its source is argument, C-3.2, where LO-21 would require the answer to stay inside the text's incidents. DEFECT: the answer is cut off by page furniture and then runs into the next exercise's instructions.

Mark each pair as fact-opinion or cause-effect AND say why -- 'it is believed' marks the opinion, the verifiable post marks the fact. C-2.2-LO-23 requires exactly that: the separation plus the test used. The concept tag 'Fact vs Opinion' agrees.

Extract on the two choices, the switch to para-athletics and the Rio silver, with the caterpillar-to-butterfly comparison. Resilience drawn from named incidents, C-2.2-LO-21. Not LO-20: the imagery here is a transformation figure, not stadium imagery.

Arrange movement words on a cline by pace -- creep, crawl, plod, amble, saunter, stroll, walk, jog, run, sprint, dart. A vocabulary exercise with no LO in this chapter (LO-24 is modals and reported speech), so C-2.2 competency. DEFECT: the stem opens with the tail of the previous answer, 'With her hard work and positive attitude, she managed to turn obstacles into stepping stones...'.

Examine how her place among the ten most inspirational para-athletes feeds the discourse on GENDER EQUALITY in sport. The student must build a case the text does not make, so C-3.2. C-2.2-LO-22 was rejected because its stereotypes are the disability ones, and this item is about a different axis.

How 'ability beyond disability' can guide future para-athletes -- the phrase C-2.2-LO-22 is written around. Not C-3.2: the answer restates and applies the text's own argument rather than weighing premises against it.
What have you learnt from this interview and how will you apply it -- a personal reflective response, C-1.2. Not C-2.1-LO-9: the form of the piece is not what is being asked about.

Complete a 'What I know / What I want to know' table on the Paralympics and SHARE the responses with classmates and teacher -- a discussion task, C-1.1. Not C-2.1-LO-10: the student is listing prior knowledge and questions, not explaining what the account records. DEFECT: the stem opens with an orphan sentence from another exercise ('Despite being severely injured early in the season...') followed by 'Downloaded from www.pdf.tube'.

The age at which she was diagnosed (29) -- one of the specific incidents of adversity the resilience theme rests on, C-2.2-LO-21. This chapter has no plain-recall outcome, and LO-21 is the outcome those incidents belong to.
The kind of tumour (spinal) -- the adversity incident, C-2.2-LO-21.
Paralysed from the WAIST down after surgery -- the adversity incident, C-2.2-LO-21. Not LO-22: no stereotype is at issue, the fact is being recalled.

Which statements are correct -- tests whether the reader has the incidents right (diagnosed at 29, true; paralysed from the neck down, false). Still the LO-21 incidents. Not LO-23: this is accuracy against the text, not fact versus opinion.
What she was told she would be bound to for life (a wheelchair) -- the prognosis she went on to defy, C-2.2-LO-21.
The two choices she faced -- squander her life in remorse, or make it a world of limitless possibilities. The pivot of the resilience theme, C-2.2-LO-21.
What she always loved (sports) -- a biographical detail that carries no adversity and no stereotype, so C-2.2 competency rather than LO-21.
What she was before her diagnosis (a swimmer) -- biographical recall, C-2.2 competency.
The field she switched to (para-athletics) -- the act of overcoming that follows the injury, C-2.2-LO-21.
Her transformation compared to a BUTTERFLY EMERGING -- the figure the text uses for coming through adversity, C-2.2-LO-21. Not LO-20, whose imagery is the stadium and the athlete in action.
The year of the breakthrough (2016) -- the turning point in the overcoming narrative, C-2.2-LO-21.

Which Games (Rio) -- the same breakthrough incident, C-2.2-LO-21. Not C-2.1-LO-10 despite the 'Paralympic Games' concept tag: LO-10 is about a change in attitudes across decades, not about where one medal was won.

Mapped on the task the answer performs: scripting an informal INTERVIEW, with questions and responses in a social setting -- C-1.1. DEFECT: the stem fuses a one-line recall question ('Which medal did she win at these Paralympic Games?') with a full list of interview prompts, and the answer addresses only the interview, so the recall question is unanswerable from the row.

What can overcome physical limitations -- strong willpower. The text's central argument for ability beyond disability, C-2.2-LO-22. Not LO-21: no specific incident is referenced, the claim is general.
Who Sheetal Devi is introduced as (a para-archer) -- recall of a detail, C-2.2 competency.
Which award she won (the Arjuna Award) -- recall, C-2.2 competency.
The year of the award (2024) -- recall, C-2.2 competency.

She shoots with her FEET -- the single clearest instance in the chapter of ability exceeding the disability, C-2.2-LO-22, and the distractors (hands, mouth, knees) make the point of the item exactly that.

Her story sets the TONE of the chapter -- a question about how the piece is built, so C-2.2 (critiquing form and style). Not C-2.1-LO-9, which asks the reader to classify the piece as non-fiction reporting and contrast its purpose with a story's; tone is not that.

The primary message of Sheetal's example -- determination helps overcome obstacles. Resilience as a theme drawn from an incident, C-2.2-LO-21. LO-22 was the alternative, but the keyed option names determination against obstacles rather than ability against disability.

The core of the chapter is an INTERVIEW with Deepa Malik -- the item tests that the reader knows what kind of text this is, which is the first half of C-2.1-LO-9 (contemporary non-fiction reporting rather than a story). The only item in this batch that asks about form.
How Dr Malik is described (a legendary Indian para-athlete) -- recall, C-2.2 competency.

Beyond her own victories she is a CHAMPION for others -- her advocacy, which is how the text presses its case against stereotypes, C-2.2-LO-22. The distractors (critic, threat, burden) are the stereotype the item is dismantling.

Who she works with on sports policy (the government) -- recall of a detail, C-2.2 competency. C-2.1-LO-10 was considered, but the item asks with whom she works, not how attitudes changed over the decades.
